chunks: 11. My father (RA) narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali the Second (AS)
“What is the meaning of al-Wahid (The One)?” He replied, “He is the One whose Divine Unity (al-Wahdaniyyah) is professed by all tongues.”

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ ال: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (AS), the second Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of al-Wahid in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Jawad (AS) defines 'al-Wahid' not merely as a numerical singularity, but as the entity whose oneness is universally confessed by all tongues, highlighting the consensus (*ijma'*) of creation. This definition underscores the comprehensiveness of Divine Unity, linking the theological concept of *Tawhid* with the experiential recognition of God by all beings. It serves as a foundational proof for the innate (*fitrah*) acknowledgment of God's unique sovereignty across diverse languages and cultures.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 1. My Father (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-`Attar said on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of Abu Hashim al-Ja`far that I asked Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn `Ali the Second (AS), “
What is the meaning of the One [al-Wahid]? He replied, “He is the One whose Divine Unity [al-Wahdaniyyah] is professed by all tongues.”
